record.field: Standard accounting Trial Balance with opening, period movement, and closing balances per account. Single SQL pass with conditional aggregation; drill down to journal items per account.
Period income statement with Income and Expenses sections plus Net Profit. Two SQL passes (one per section) with the standard filter set; drill down to journal items per account.

Cumulative point in time snapshot at date_to with Assets, Liabilities, Equity sections, plus Current Year Earnings, Total Liabilities and Equity, and an automatic Balance Check that surfaces any drift in the underlying ledger.

Per account ledger with opening balance, every journal item in the period (date, journal, move, partner, label, debit, credit, running balance), and an account total. Drill down: account headers open the journal items list filtered to that account; entry rows open the specific journal entry form.

Per partner ledger with opening balance, every journal item in the period attached to that partner, and a partner total. Drill down: partner headers open the journal items list filtered to that partner; entry rows open the specific journal entry form.
Open customer balances at date_to bucketed by days overdue (Not Due, 0 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90, 91 plus). Drill down: each partner row opens the open journal items list filtered to that partner.

Open vendor balances at date_to bucketed by days overdue. Same five bucket layout as Aged Receivable but scoped to liability_payable accounts and signed so the displayed amounts represent what the company owes.

Direct method Cash Flow Statement: classifies cash affecting moves into Operating, Investing, and Financing activities by inspecting non cash counterparts. Includes Opening Cash, Closing Cash, and a Balance Check that verifies Closing equals Opening plus Net Change.

Per-partner statement of open invoices and recent payments on the receivable account, ordered by date with a running balance and a final amount due. Driven by the same partial-reconcile rewind as the aged report so a back-dated statement reflects what was open on that date.
Mirror of the customer statement on the payable side: open vendor bills and payments with a running balance and the amount the company currently owes the vendor.

Net analytic impact per analytic account. Allocation-percentage weighted; income negated so positive rows mean net cost on the analytic and negative rows mean net contribution. One section per analytic plan.
